approved: The majority voted against a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?id=2025-02-10.8.2) introduced by Tasmanian Senator [Jonathon Duniam](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/senate/tasmania/jonathon_duniam) (Liberal), which means it failed. ### Motion text > *That so much of standing orders be suspended as would prevent me from moving a motion to provide for the consideration of a matter, namely a motion to give precedence to a motion relating to the consideration of the [Defence Service Homes Amendment (Insurance) Bill 2025](https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/Bills_Search_Results/Result?bId=r7304).*

Moved to suspend standing orders and prioritise the Defence Service Homes Amendment (Insurance) Bill 2025, arguing it was urgent for affected veterans, including people impacted by flooding around Townsville; the government opposed rearranging the program, saying the bill could pass after Future Made in Australia legislation.

Invited the opposition to support changing the Senate program so the Defence Service Homes Amendment (Insurance) Bill 2025 and the FMIAbill could be considered and passed today, with the Senate sitting later if necessary.

Moved procedural motions to vary the Senate's hours and limit debate, including votes on the Future Made in Australia (Production Tax Credits and Other Measures) Bill 2024 at 8 pm and the Defence Service Homes Amendment (Insurance) Bill 2025 at 9 pm; debate criticised the government's handling of scrutiny and supported proceeding with both bills.

Supported the Defence Service Homes Amendment (Insurance) Bill 2025, describing it as non-controversial and necessary to resolve insurance authority issues affecting defence personnel, veterans and families. The debate also sought transparency about retrospectively validating Commonwealth activities since 1990, while the minister said the bill would formalise authority, validate past activities and support more than 32,000 current policyholders. The bill passed its second reading.
